substantive_reconstruction.finite_positive_route: For finite G over C, h_G(v,w)=|G|^-1 sum h(rho(g)v,rho(g)w) is Hermitian and sesquilinear. At v!=0 each rho(g)v is nonzero, so positivity is strict. Reindexing g->gk proves invariance. If W is invariant, group inverses preserve W too, and h_G(rho(k)u,w)=h_G(u,rho(k)^-1w)=0 makes W-perp invariant. Finite dimension gives the direct sum and permits induction to irreducibles. The zero-space induction base is harmless; no nonexistent nonzero vector is used there. The argument is explicitly complex/Hermitian, not a theorem over modular fields; the separate order-invertibility condition for algebraic Maschke is correctly noted.
substantive_reconstruction.compact_conditional_route: For continuous finite-dimensional rho and normalized Haar probability, the squared norm of rho(g)v is a continuous strictly positive function on compact G for each fixed v!=0. It attains a strictly positive minimum because action maps are invertible. Thus the integral is definite, and right invariance gives the same metric/complement proof. The usual Haar setting and continuity/integrability are actual conditions of this positive subtheorem, not promises about every abstract action in the question. Haar existence is an explicit external dependency; neither source inspection nor this proof establishes it.
substantive_reconstruction.infinite_measure_boundary: On R, translation-invariant Borel probability would assign the same mass c to every[n,n+1). Countable additivity makes c>0 incompatible with finite mass and c0 incompatible with total mass1. This refutes the proposed probability route, not every possible averaging process. A trivial R-action remains unitary. The answer therefore avoids the false inference that noncompactness alone makes each representation nonunitarizable.
substantive_reconstruction.continuous_shear_and_all_complements: With N=E12, N^2=0 gives rho(s)rho(t)=I+(s+t)N and inverse rho(-t); entries are continuous. W=Ce1 is invariant. Every vector-space complement in C^2 must be a line generated by(a,b) with b!=0. Its invariance would give(a+tb,b)=lambda_t(a,b), hence lambda_t=1 and, using t1, b0: contradiction. The same equations exclude every other invariant line. This proves non-complete-reducibility rather than merely reducibility. An invariant definite metric would provide the impossible W-perp complement, proving nonunitarizability separately. The positive quadratic coefficient in ||t e1+e2||_h^2 is a consistent second check.
substantive_reconstruction.compact_hamel_and_L1_discriminator: For irrational alpha, {1,alpha} is Q-independent; extend it to a Hamel basis and define L(1)=0,L(alpha)=1. The additive map ell([x])=L(x) on R/Z is well defined since integer shifts have L0. Sigma=I+ell N is an invertible representation, with a nontrivial shear at[alpha], so the same all-complement proof applies. Ell([n alpha])=n is unbounded, excluding continuity on a compact domain. More strongly, if ell were Haar-L1, translation by[alpha] and ell(x+[alpha])=ell(x)+1 would force integral ell=integral ell+1. Thus its nonintegrability is proved directly, without an unproved measurable-homomorphism automatic-continuity theorem or a computational interpretation of Hamel choice.
